memories.content: The user's mother's birthday falls in the third week of January.
At the user's last family meal out, noise from the next table made conversation nearly impossible.
At a barbecue at home in the same month, the user was comfortable because no one had to raise their voice.
During their mother's birthday meal, the user left a restaurant with loud music after 30 minutes.
When discussing postponed matters with family, the user prefers a quiet, one-on-one dining environment.
At a large banquet hall reserved by their older sister, the user remembered the surrounding noise more than the food.
On a day the user ate grilled food at home with their younger brother, conversation was easy to continue, so the user stayed another hour after the meal.
The user's mother considers having the whole family eat at the same time more important than receiving a birthday gift.

When proposing a birthday meal for the user's mother, check the schedule and attendees; if conversation is the purpose, first consider a low-noise location, then confirm the final choice with the user.
The local agent can compare past dining environments and the user's responses, but those records alone cannot determine the location of the next gathering.
The user keeps waterproof shoes for rainy days to the left of the entrance.
On a day the user walked in the rain wearing thin shoes, their socks became wet and they changed them after arrival.
On the next rainy day, the user wore waterproof shoes and their feet remained dry.
On a day the user walked for a long time in new shoes, their heel chafed and they shortened the route home.
The user wore the same shoes on two short outings before using them on a long walk.
On a day the user dried an umbrella outside the entrance, they found it immediately before the next outing.
On a day the user put a folded wet umbrella in their bag, documents inside became wet.
When rain is forecast, the user's mother expects the user may forget an umbrella and sets out a spare at the entrance.
When proposing a long-distance walking plan, check both the weather that day and recent records of shoe discomfort.
Even if the local agent knows a shoe's location, it cannot know its current condition or whether it is usable.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate practical domains: family birthday dining and rainy-weather walking preparation. Neither supplies an operational claim about the other domain, so their independently useful preferences, experiences, planning guidance, and agent limitations remain distinct without conflict.
